Proximal Operator of a Separable Penalty

Source: R/prox.R
penalty_prox.DistribPenalty.Rd

Computes closed forms for the Gaussian, the Laplace (in both parametrizations) and the elastic net, and for every other parent with a differentiable log-density it computes the stationary point of smallest objective, coordinate by coordinate. A diagonal map is handled by rescaling, and any other map is rejected.

Arguments

penalty

A DistribPenalty() object.

v

A numeric vector of length penalty@n_coef.

step

The step length \(t\), a single positive finite number.

theta

A named list of hyperparameter values.

...

Unused, and accepted so that the signature matches the generic's.

Value

A numeric vector of the same length as v.

The closed forms

parentoperator
gaussian1\((v - t g_0)/(1 + t/\sigma^2)\), with \(g_0\) the gradient at the origin
laplace, laplace2\(\mathrm{sign}(v)(\lvert v\rvert - t\lambda)_{+}\)
enetthe soft threshold at \(t\lambda\alpha\), then division by \(1 + t\lambda(1-\alpha)\)

For the laplace parametrization \(\lambda = 1/\sigma\). The two steps of the elastic net follow from one stationary condition: \((\beta - v)/t + a\,\mathrm{sign}(\beta) + c\beta = 0\), with \(a = \lambda\alpha\) and \(c = \lambda(1-\alpha)\), separates into the threshold of the Laplace part followed by the shrinkage of the Gaussian part.

The location of the parent

The Laplace and elastic-net forms are written for a parent centered at zero, and the family name does not carry the location. The gradient of the penalty at the origin is therefore evaluated, and the call signals an error when its largest absolute entry exceeds \(10^{-8}\max(1, \lambda)\). The Gaussian form has no such restriction, because the location enters the stationary condition linearly and is carried through as \(g_0\).

Parents without a closed form

Any other parent is solved coordinate by coordinate from \((\beta - v)/t = \ell^{(y)}(\beta)\), whose right-hand side is distributions7::distrib_grad_y(). The condition can have more than one root when the density is not log-concave, so every change of sign on the segment between \(v\) and the mode of the parent is refined and the root of smallest objective is returned, as .prox_root() describes. That root is the global minimizer when the parent is unimodal, and a stationary point that need not be the global minimizer when the parent has more than one mode. A parent that declares a kink and is not one of the closed-form families is rejected, because the stationary condition does not hold at a kink and the minimizer of such a penalty can lie there.

Errors

A parent read in blocks, a map that is not a Matrix diagonal object with nonzero entries, a Laplace or elastic-net parent that is not centered at zero, a parent that declares a kink and has no closed form, and a stationary condition with no change of sign on the segment or in the widened bracket each signal an error with a message giving the reason; all but the off-center parent name the penalty.

See also

penalty_prox() for the generic, distrib_penalty() for the branch, distributions7::distrib_grad_y() for the root's right-hand side.

Examples

v <- c(2, 0.3, -1.4)

# The soft threshold sets everything within t * lambda of zero to zero.
penalty_prox(lasso_penalty(n_coef = 3), v, 1, list(lambda = 1))
#> [1]  1.0  0.0 -0.4

# The elastic net thresholds first and then shrinks what survives.
penalty_prox(elasticnet_penalty(n_coef = 3), v, 1,
             list(lambda = 1, alpha = 0.6))
#> [1]  1.0000000  0.0000000 -0.5714286
sign(v) * pmax(abs(v) - 1 * 1 * 0.6, 0) / (1 + 1 * 1 * (1 - 0.6))
#> [1]  1.0000000  0.0000000 -0.5714286

# A Student t prior has no closed form, and the operator is found from the
# stationary condition. With sigma = 1, nu = 4 and step 1 it maps 2 to 1,
# as the ridge with lambda = 1 does; the two differ for coordinates that
# are large relative to sigma, such as 10.
v2 <- c(2, 0.3, 10)
penalty_prox(heavy_penalty(n_coef = 3), v2, 1, list(sigma = 1, nu = 4))
#> [1] 1.0000000 0.1336635 9.4958181
penalty_prox(ridge_penalty(n_coef = 3), v2, 1, list(lambda = 1))
#> [1] 1.00 0.15 5.00
